definitions.explanation: Japanese sweets with a moisture content between fresh ({生菓子|なまがし}) and dry ({干菓子|ひがし}) wagashi. Includes most {最中|もなか} and many bean-jam-filled pastries; keeps longer than fresh wagashi.

examples.japanese: {半生菓子|はんなまがし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日持|ひも}ち→日持ち：12886_himochi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧よい。
⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{半生菓子|はんなまがし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ→詰め合わせ：14175_tsumeawase⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}んだ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
examples.english: I chose an assortment of semi-dry wagashi as a souvenir.

examples.japanese: {半生菓子|はんなまがし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{水分量|すいぶんりょう}⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧⟦{生菓子|なまがし}→生菓子：27039_namagashi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{干菓子|ひがし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中間|ちゅうかん}→中間：05458_chuukan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分類|ぶんるい}される→分類する：25224_bunruisuru⟧。
examples.english: Semi-dry wagashi are classified between fresh and dry wagashi based on moisture content.

notes:
Industry term used by wagashi makers and packaged-food labels. Defined by water content: roughly 10–30%, between fresh wagashi (above 30%) and dry wagashi (below 10%). Because of the lower moisture, {半生菓子|はんなまがし} tolerate gift-shop shelf lives of one to two weeks.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{生菓子|なまがし}→生菓子：27039_namagashi⟧: fresh wagashi — must be eaten within a day or two
- {干菓子|ひがし}: dry wagashi — keeps for months ({落雁|らくがん}, candies)
- {上生菓子|じょうなまがし}: high-grade fresh wagashi — formal tea sweets
